IELTS Speaking 1-to-1 with Mr. Jay JURASSIC ENGLISH ™
5Jurassic English · jurassicenglish.com © Jurassic English
The Full Ladder: 110 Seconds
Length: 60 minutes · one teacher, one student · Google Meet
Goal: the student adds Rung 4, LAND IT, and speaks a full Part 2 for at least 90 seconds without help.
Assumes: an earlier lesson taught -ed endings you can hear, the before/after bridge and keeping a story in
the past tense.
Rules: the stopwatch is the record; the student writes their own numbers. Praise quotes the student's exact
sentence. One ﬁx at a time. No band is given in a lesson.
The
ladder
Rung Time What
the
student
does
1 SET IT 15 s who, what, when
2 ANCHOR IT 40 s a quote and a sense detail
3 WIDEN IT 35 s before, after, compare
4 LAND IT 20 s what it taught you, then a closing sentence
Total 110
s the ﬂoor is 90 s; the target is 110 s
Lesson
plan
Step Time What
happens How
it
is
measured
1 · Your target 0:00 · 3
min
The student writes their longest Part 2 so far and says a target
for today. The ﬂoor is 90 seconds and the target is 110.
Target written by the
student
2 · Cold
check: the last
sound
0:03 · 3
min
No teaching ﬁrst. The teacher says 10 verbs (hurry, decide,
stop, carry, start, ask, want, close, jump, miss), one every 10
seconds. The student says each one in the past and holds the
last sound.
Endings clearly heard, out
of 10 (target 8)
3 · Cold
check: stay in
the past
0:06 · 3
min
"Tell me about the last time you visited a friend's or a relative's
house." 45 seconds. Then a tick or a cross for each check.
Present-tense slips in the
story (target 2 or fewer)
4 · Fix only
what failed
0:09 · 5
min
Only the crosses are ﬁxed. Endings: /t/ walked · /d/ planned · /
ɪd/ needed, then the missed words again. Past lane: "Stay in
the past until 'Now…' or 'If…'." The student re-tells the part
that failed.
Missed words repaired;
story re-told
5 · The full
ladder and
Rung 4
0:14 · 5
min
The four rungs and their clocks. Then the closing frames:
"Looking back, …" · "That taught me …" · "If I could do it
again, I would …" · "Now I always …". Never end with "That's
all."
The student names the four
rungs and says each frame
once
6 · LAND IT
drill
0:19 · 3
min
Two closing sentences for each story, 20 seconds each: you
forgot a friend's birthday · you broke your phone screen on a
school trip · you waited for a friend who forgot to come.
Closing sentences, out of 3

7 · Practice
card: plan
0:22 · 2

"Describe a time you waited a long time for something." One
minute to write four words, one for each rung.
Plan made, yes or no
8 · Rung walk 0:24 · 8
min
The student speaks one rung at a time. The teacher stops at
each clock (15, 40, 35, 20 seconds), praises one exact
sentence and gives one ﬁx. A short rung is said again at once.
Seconds per rung against
15 / 40 / 35 / 20
9 · Listen for
the change
0:32 · 5
min
Three short messages read once. Each has a change of plan
("Actually, let's make it ten"). The student says the ﬁnal answer
in a full sentence and the word that signalled the change.
Final answers, out of 3
10 · Part 3:
answer ﬁrst
0:37 · 5
min
Two questions: "Why are some people always late?" and "Is it
more important to be on time at work or at school? Why?"
Answer ﬁrst, then a reason, an example and a closing
sentence.
Four moves heard; 30–45
seconds each
11 · Exam
rules and a
new card
0:42 · 3
min
A card the student has not seen: "Describe a time you were
late for something important." One minute of notes, four
words.
Notes made
12 · Speak: up
to 2 minutes
0:45 · 3
min
No help, no prompts. The teacher says nothing until 2:00 or
until the student stops, then waits 5 seconds.
Total seconds (ﬂoor 90,
target 110); rung reached
13 · Your
result
0:48 · 2
min
The student writes the time, the rung reached and their closing
sentence. "Where did I stop? What was I going to say next?"
Numbers written by the
student
14 · Go again 0:50 · 4
min
Same story, longer and better, using the answer to "What was
I going to say next?"
Second time against the
ﬁrst (aim: 15 seconds more)
15 · Close and
practice at
home
0:54 · 6
min
The student says one thing done well (a sentence from today)
and one thing still short (a number). The teacher goes through
the printable lesson handout for practice at home.
Home practice understood

short: shorten step 9, then step 6. Never cut steps 8, 12 or 14.
